newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMANS WANT BIG CUTS IN EURO 2000 QUALIFYING GAMES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMANS WANT BIG CUTS IN EURO 2000 QUALIFYING GAMES.

text.p: European champions Germany said on Friday they would propose a big cut in the number of qualification matches for the next European championship in the year 2000.

German soccer federation chief Egidius Braun, who is also vice-president of Europe's governing body UEFA, said he would urge a UEFA meeting next week to reduce the number of matches each country has to play by increasing the qualifying groups from eight to 14.
Instead of qualifying groups of six teams, the groups would be reduced to three or four teams, cutting the number of matches for each country from 10 to four or six.
This would allow countries more time for lucrative friendly matches. The 2000 tournament is being staged jointly by the Netherlands and Belgium.
"I will propose to the executive committee on Thursday in Tenerife that that there be 14 groups with only the winner qualifying for the finals," Braun said.
Germany, however, are sticking by their decision not to play in the new "mini" World Cup to be contested for the first time in December next year in Saudi Arabia.
Earlier this month world governing body FIFA gave the go-ahead for the inaugural Confederations Cup which will be contested every two years by continental champions.
The event clashes with the start of the winter break in Germany.
Braun said: "We could sent a B team but that would be an insult to the organisers."
